1_parties_and_buyer_credit.value: Seller is Havrebakke Vind ApS and Buyer is Jutland Board & Packaging A/S, both Danish companies. The Buyer's payment obligations are guaranteed by Jutland Industri Holding A/S under a Parent Company Guarantee (Annex 4). The Buyer has no rating from a recognised rating agency.
1_parties_and_buyer_credit.quote: The Buyer's payment obligations under this Agreement are guaranteed by Jutland Industri Holding A/S under the Parent Company Guarantee set out in Annex 4.
1_parties_and_buyer_credit.clause: Part I, Parties; section 9.2; section 9.5; Annex 4
1_parties_and_buyer_credit.note: The document is an unsigned draft of 12 March 2026 and the guarantee is dated [date of signing]. The guarantee has no cap of its own: its liability is limited to the Buyer's liability under the Agreement (Annex 4, para 5). The Guarantor's own credit standing or rating is not stated. The only trigger is section 9.5: if the Guarantor stops holding the Buyer's entire share capital, or the guarantee lapses, the Buyer must replace it or double the Letter of Credit within 20 Business Days.

2_facility.value: Onshore wind farm with eight turbine generators and a total installed capacity of 48.0 MW, at Havrebakke in Ringkøbing-Skjern Municipality, Denmark, in bidding zone DK1.
2_facility.quote: The Facility is the Havrebakke Wind Farm, consisting of eight onshore wind turbine generators with a total installed capacity of 48.0 MW located at Havrebakke in Ringkøbing-Skjern Municipality, Denmark, in bidding zone DK1, together with the internal cabling, the Havrebakke substation and the ancillary installations described in Annex 1.
2_facility.note: Annex 1 gives 6.0 MW per turbine, a 125 m hub height and a 162 m rotor diameter. Only one capacity figure is given and it is not labelled AC or DC.

3_supply_period.value: Ten years, starting on the Commercial Operation Date.
3_supply_period.quote: Supply Period: ten (10) years commencing on the Commercial Operation Date.
3_supply_period.clause: Part I, Supply Period; section 1.1 (Commercial Operation Date); section 3.3
3_supply_period.note: The Commercial Operation Date is the date the Seller notifies the Buyer that the section 3.3 conditions are met: all eight turbines commissioned, grid connection and meters verified, and registrations done. It is not a fixed calendar date.

4_cod_and_delay.value: Target Commercial Operation Date is 1 October 2027 and the Longstop Date is 31 December 2027. Delay liquidated damages are EUR 9,600 per day, capped at EUR 1,750,000 in aggregate.
4_cod_and_delay.quote: If the Commercial Operation Date has not occurred by the Target Commercial Operation Date of 1 October 2027, the Seller shall pay the Buyer liquidated damages of EUR 9,600 for each day of delay, up to an aggregate cap of EUR 1,750,000.
4_cod_and_delay.clause: Part I, Supply Period; section 3.4; section 3.5; section 3.6; Annex 1 (construction schedule)
4_cod_and_delay.note: Both dates are extended day for day for Force Majeure or Buyer breach, up to 180 days in aggregate (3.5). The liquidated damages are the Buyer's sole remedy for delay apart from the right to terminate if the Longstop Date, as extended, is missed (3.4, 3.6).

5_price_and_indexation.value: EUR 58.00 per MWh, exclusive of VAT, applied to each MWh of Metered Output from the Commercial Operation Date. Indexation: none, the price is fixed for the Supply Period.
5_price_and_indexation.quote: Contract Price: EUR 58.00 per MWh, exclusive of value added tax, applicable to each MWh of Metered Output from the Commercial Operation Date.
5_price_and_indexation.clause: Annex 2 (Election Sheet); referenced from Part I, Price and section 7.1
5_price_and_indexation.note: The price is stated only in Annex 2, not in the body. There is no indexation start date or share because Annex 2 says indexation is none. Part I and section 7.1 say the price can be adjusted only as provided in Annex 2, but section 11.2 allows a Change in Law adjustment of the Contract Price by negotiation. The document does not reconcile the two.

6_volume_and_performance.value: Pay-as-produced: the Buyer takes 100% of Metered Output. Expected Annual Production is 158,000 MWh (P50) and Minimum Annual Production is 118,500 MWh (75% of P50). If Metered Output falls short in a Contract Year, the Seller pays the shortfall in MWh times any excess of the average DK1 day-ahead price over the Contract Price, capped at EUR 500,000 per Contract Year.
6_volume_and_performance.quote: If in any Contract Year the Metered Output is less than the Minimum Annual Production, the Seller shall pay the Buyer a shortfall payment equal to the shortfall in MWh multiplied by the amount, if positive, by which the average day-ahead price for bidding zone DK1 for that Contract Year exceeds the Contract Price, capped at EUR 500,000 per Contract Year.
6_volume_and_performance.clause: Part I, Contract Quantity and Volume Structure; sections 4.1, 4.3, 4.5, 4.6; Annex 1; Annex 2
6_volume_and_performance.note: The minimum is reduced pro rata in the first and last Contract Year. It is also reduced by output lost to Force Majeure, grid-operator output reductions or Buyer breach, calculated under 5.5. The shortfall payment is zero when the DK1 day-ahead price is at or below EUR 58.00. There is no separate availability guarantee: the 97% availability in Annex 1 is an input to the P50 estimate. Section 4.3 says the P50 is used only for sections 9.2 and 13.3.

7_product_and_certificates.value: Electricity delivered at the Delivery Point plus all Guarantees of Origin issued for the Metered Output, transferred to the Buyer at no additional cost. No capacity product, ancillary service or other attribute is sold.
7_product_and_certificates.quote: Product: electricity generated by the Facility and delivered at the Delivery Point, together with all Guarantees of Origin issued in respect of the Metered Output.
7_product_and_certificates.clause: Part I, Product and Certificates; sections 8.1–8.3
7_product_and_certificates.note: The Seller transfers the certificates monthly, within 15 Business Days of issue. It need not procure replacement certificates for any production shortfall (8.2). Certificates under a replacement scheme are also transferred at no additional cost (8.3).

8_curtailment.value: Grid-operator (TSO) instructed output reductions give rise to no payment by the Buyer, so they are not paid as deemed delivery, and any TSO compensation belongs to the Seller. Such reductions only lower the Minimum Annual Production used in the shortfall test.
8_curtailment.quote: Reductions of output instructed by the transmission system operator shall not give rise to any payment by the Buyer.
8_curtailment.note: The lost quantity is calculated from met-mast wind, the turbine power curve, turbine availability and losses (5.5). The document gives the Buyer no right to curtail and states no cap in hours or MWh. It does not address negative prices. The Buyer must take 100% of Metered Output (4.1).

9_delivery_point_and_balancing.value: Physical settlement. The Delivery Point is the metering point on the 60 kV side of the Havrebakke substation, where title and risk pass to the Buyer. The Buyer appoints the balance responsible party and bears all imbalance costs from the Commercial Operation Date.
9_delivery_point_and_balancing.quote: The Buyer shall appoint the balance responsible party for the Facility and shall bear all imbalance costs from the Commercial Operation Date.
9_delivery_point_and_balancing.clause: Part I, Settlement; Part I, Delivery Point and Balancing; sections 4.2, 5.2; Annex 2
9_delivery_point_and_balancing.note: No reference price applies because settlement is physical, not financial. The Seller supplies day-ahead and intraday production forecasts without warranty (5.1).

10_credit_support.value: Seller: a bank guarantee of EUR 2,000,000 delivered within 10 Business Days after Financial Close, in force until 12 months after the Commercial Operation Date. Buyer: the Parent Company Guarantee, plus a letter of credit for six months of expected payments (six twelfths of Expected Annual Production times the Contract Price), delivered at least 30 days before the expected Commercial Operation Date and in force until 60 days after the Supply Period ends.
10_credit_support.quote: The Buyer shall deliver a letter of credit in an amount equal to six (6) months of expected payments under this Agreement, calculated as six twelfths of the Expected Annual Production multiplied by the Contract Price in force at the time of calculation, no later than thirty (30) days before the expected Commercial Operation Date, to remain in force until sixty (60) days after the end of the Supply Period.
10_credit_support.clause: Part I, Credit Support; sections 9.1–9.5; Annex 2; Annex 3; Annex 4
10_credit_support.note: The letter of credit amount is recalculated each 1 January. At EUR 58.00 and 158,000 MWh it is about EUR 4.58 million; this figure is computed here and not stated in the document. Both banks must be rated at least A-. A lost rating or missing renewal must be fixed within 20 Business Days, failing which the full amount can be drawn as cash security (9.4). The Parent Company Guarantee stays in force until all Buyer payments are made (Annex 4, para 6).

11_default_and_termination.value: Events of Default include non-payment (10 Business Days after notice), failure to deliver, restore or replace credit support (10 Business Days), insolvency, an uncured material breach (30 days) and assignment in breach. For the Seller they also include missing the Longstop Date or selling to a third party; for the Buyer, Guarantor insolvency or lapse of the guarantee. The Termination Amount is the present value of the difference between the Contract Price and the Reference Forward Price over the remainder of the Supply Period for the Expected Annual Production, discounted at the Danish central bank rate plus 2 percentage points. The Non-Defaulting Party determines it, and it is payable only if it is a loss for that party.
11_default_and_termination.quote: The Termination Amount shall be the present value of the difference between the Contract Price and the Reference Forward Price for the Expected Annual Production over the remainder of the Supply Period, discounted at the reference rate of the Danish central bank plus two (2) percentage points, and determined by the Non-Defaulting Party as at the early termination date, acting in good faith and in a commercially reasonable manner.
11_default_and_termination.clause: Section 12.1; section 13.2–13.6; section 1.1 (Reference Forward Price); Annex 2 (production profile factor 0.88)
11_default_and_termination.note: The calculation is fully specified in the attached document. The Reference Forward Price uses quotes from at least three market participants chosen by the Non-Defaulting Party, adjusted by the 0.88 factor in Annex 2. Section 12.1(f) makes missing the Longstop Date an Event of Default, but 3.6 and 13.6 say no Termination Amount is payable on a longstop termination. The document does not reconcile the two; 13.6 appears to govern. The Termination Amount is the exclusive remedy for loss of bargain (13.5).

12_change_in_law_and_force_majeure.value: If a Change in Law raises a Party's cost of performance by more than EUR 250,000 in a Contract Year, the Parties negotiate an adjustment in good faith, which may include the Contract Price. If none is agreed within 90 days, the affected Party may terminate on 60 days' notice with no Termination Amount. Force Majeure lasting more than 180 consecutive days lets either Party terminate on 30 days' notice, also with no Termination Amount.
12_change_in_law_and_force_majeure.quote: If a Change in Law increases the cost to a Party of performing this Agreement by more than EUR 250,000 in any Contract Year, the Parties shall negotiate in good faith an adjustment to restore the economic balance of this Agreement, which may include an adjustment to the Contract Price.
12_change_in_law_and_force_majeure.note: No single party bears Change in Law cost. Below the threshold it stays with the party that bears the relevant tax or charge under 17.2: the Seller for generation and injection, the Buyer for offtake, transport, consumption and resale. 17.3 applies section 11 to new taxes above the threshold. Excluded from Change in Law: corporate income tax of general application and changes published in final form before signing. The 11.2 price adjustment sits uneasily with Annex 2, which fixes the price and excludes indexation; the document does not reconcile them.
